encounters.prompt: show me when voyager 1 flew past jupiter
encounters.gpu: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Max, Unspecified Version)
encounters.reply:
Voyager 1's closest approach to Jupiter was on 1979-03-05 at about 12:04 UTC. The center-to-center range was about 348,892 km. The viewer is now paused at that moment, tracking Voyager 1 with Jupiter and the spacecraft both in frame.

I computed this from the loaded SPICE kernels. The search covered 1978-06-15 to 1980-01-14 with no light-time correction and a 1-hour step, and it returned only the deepest approach in that window.

limitations: Results apply only to the loaded kernel set and declared window. Search step limits completeness.
Context frame is analysis metadata; scalar range is frame independent. Calculation frames are declared by the event kind.
3D event geometry uses rendered trajectories/positions; it is explanatory, not a second GF calculation.
Draw-enabled glyphs/spans do not guarantee unoccluded pixels or calibrated geometry. This read does not move the camera; projected participant centers report the actual current view.

encounters.prompt: show cassini at closest approach to mimas
encounters.gpu: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4 Max, Unspecified Version)
encounters.reply:
The viewer now shows Cassini at its closest approach to Mimas, at 2004-07-01 00:30:12 UTC. The centre-to-centre range is about 76,686 km, or about 76,487 km altitude. I paused the clock there and framed Cassini and Mimas together. Both are in view, but this doesn't prove they are unoccluded.

I searched 2004-01-02 to 2005-04-07 with no light-time correction and a 1-hour step, using SPICE kernel data. The query was set to return only the deepest approach, so it doesn't list other, more distant passes. A 1-hour step can also miss a very short minimum.

naturalPoint.prompt: can you place a point then
naturalPoint.reply:
I saved one point in a new layer on Mars called "Ingenuity pick marker" and selected it. The viewer shows the layer as visible. Its drawing group is observed, with one feature, and terrain coverage was not assessed.

The point is at 77.448° E, 18.433° N planetocentric, in the IAU_MARS frame. I took those coordinates from the earlier pin, which was placed at 2021-07-05 09:00 UTC. It's a snapshot and won't follow Ingenuity. The pin is still in place.

The feature list shows no name for the point, so my "Ingenuity ground point" label may not have been stored.
naturalPoint.laterChange: Final read summary clarifies privacy-withheld names do not mean a failed label save; covered by geographic-agent-metadata regression. An additional paid rerun was not executed because automatic approval review returned model-capacity errors.
